facts.text: I have pain in my left elbow.
It's at the back of the elbow.
It came on suddenly about a year ago.
It started when I was sitting on the ground and leaned back onto my hand on something hard, so my weight pushed through the arm with the elbow straight and bent backwards.
It was severe when it happened.
It has never gone away; it's been going on for a year now.
It hurts when I straighten my elbow all the way.
Since the injury my elbow catches when I bend and straighten it.

findings.name: elbow examination
findings.result: Left elbow extension limited to 5°, compared with 10° on the right; full extension of the left elbow elicits posterior tenderness and palpable crepitus.

findings.name: elbow ligament stability testing
findings.result: No instability of the ulnar collateral ligament or the lateral ulnar collateral ligament.

findings.name: MRI of the left elbow
findings.result: Hypertrophied posterior fat pad interposed between the olecranon and the olecranon fossa.

findings.name: MRI of the right elbow
findings.result: Similarly hypertrophied posterior fat pad, although positioned less inferiorly.

aliases: posterior impingement caused by a hypertrophied posterior fat pad
posterior fat pad impingement of the elbow
gold.reasoning: 1. Ligamentous instability (ulnar or lateral ulnar collateral) was considered as a mechanism for posterior impingement — “our patient showed no instability of these ligaments.” 2. Hypertrophied posterior fat pad impingement was supported by imaging findings — “This constellation of clinical symptoms and imaging findings was compatible with posterior impingement caused by a hypertrophied posterior fat pad.”
